For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the eggplant came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-eggplant" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-eggplant-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of eggplant, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for eggplant, as sold on this basis in the completed eggplant ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" class="internal" data-slug="sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants" data-no-cite-meta>WHO GEMS/Food</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>2 sampling families with different designs; none is a probability sample of world supply. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/ahmed2024-erbil-local-imported-vegetables-xrf" class="internal" data-slug="sources/ahmed2024-erbil-local-imported-vegetables-xrf" data-no-cite-meta>Ahmed 2024</a></li><li><a href="../sources/sultana2021-dhaka-kawran-bazar-fruit-vegetables-metals" class="internal" data-slug="sources/sultana2021-dhaka-kawran-bazar-fruit-vegetables-metals" data-no-cite-meta>Sultana et al. 2021</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. <a id="sources-and-contamination-pathways"></a>
## How metals reach eggplant

<a id="hmi-ing-010"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-root-uptake-surface-deposition-feed-transfer-or-other-biological-pathways"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-011"></a>
<a id="what-contamination-can-arise-from-agricultural-inputs-harvesting-processing-equipment-or-packaging"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-012"></a>
<a id="which-source-attribution-claims-are-measured-modelled-inferred-or-unresolved"></a>

The evidence on how metals reach eggplant comes from studies that compared exposed and ordinary settings. Eggplant, as sold from Location B1 (industrial-affected area) had total mercury higher at 43.4 µg/kg, against 0.43 µg/kg for Control (grocery store >55 km from any power plant) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

These are observational comparisons from single studies; the size of the difference depends on the site, metal and distance.

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, eggplant, as sold had the lowest cadmium subgroup median in EMRO (3.91 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (39 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

In one study, lead across 6 groups of eggplant ranged from 260 µg/kg (Sesh More (SM) bazar, occasion 3) to 300 µg/kg (Kamal Ranjit (KR) market, occasion 3); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/mostafa2023-mymensingh-market-vegetables-lead-cadmium|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Mostafa F, Goswami C, Chacrabati R · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/mostafa2023-mymensingh-market-vegetables-lead-cadmium">Assessment of lead (Pb) and cadmium (Cd) contamination in locally available vegetables in Mymensingh</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Journal of Agriculture, Food and Environment 4(4):20-23</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/mostafa2023-mymensingh-market-vegetables-lead-cadmium">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In another study, lead across 4 groups of eggplant ranged from 1,200 µg/kg (Nelamangala taluk market, Bangalore Rural) to 8,200 µg/kg (Doddaballapura taluk market, Bangalore Rural); the lowest is the lowest observed in that study, not an established sourcing preference.<sup class="cite">[[sources/shivakumar2020-bangalore-vegetables-fruits-metals|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Shivakumar L, Reddy KR, Kalshetty BM · 2020</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/shivakumar2020-bangalore-vegetables-fruits-metals">Heavy Metal Contaminations and Health Risk Assessment from Fruits and Vegetables in Bangalore Rural Markets, Karnataka, India</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Rasayan Journal of Chemistry, Vol. 13, No. 4, 2498-2507</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/shivakumar2020-bangalore-vegetables-fruits-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-eggplant" data-anchor="how-do-heavy-metals-get-into-eggplant" data-question="How do heavy metals get into eggplant?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>How do heavy metals get into eggplant?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

In the studies available, eggplant from contaminated or exposed settings carried more metal than eggplant from the same study’s control.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Eggplant, as sold from Location A1 (industrial-affected area) had total mercury higher at 42.4 µg/kg, against 0.43 µg/kg for Control (grocery store >55 km from any power plant) in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">
